questions: Is the total cost the sum of the costs of each swap operation performed, or is it the minimum possible total cost to sort the permutation?
When swapping P_i and P_{i+1}, does the cost i refer to the index before the swap or after the swap if indices shift due to previous swaps?
Are we allowed to perform swaps in any order, and does the cost depend on the current state of the permutation or only on the fixed index i chosen?
Does 'ascending order' mean P_1 < P_2 < ... < P_N, or is it sorted according to the values 1..N?
If multiple sequences of swaps achieve sorting, should we output the minimum total cost among them, or any valid total cost?
Is the cost i an integer cost, and should the total cost be computed as an integer sum without overflow issues given constraints?
Can we choose the same i multiple times in succession, and does the cost remain i each time?
Does the operation require that i is within bounds 1 ≤ i ≤ N-1 at the time of each operation, considering N is fixed?
